operators.notes: Stream shared lineitem scan; for each row where l_commitdate < l_receiptdate, set bit at l_orderkey. Parallel: each thread processes morsels into thread-local bitset, then OR-merge. Result is a single bitset of qualifying orderkeys.
Scan orders with zonemap pruning on o_orderdate. Block size 65536, ~229 blocks; expect ~8 qualifying blocks. Read only o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_orderpriority columns.
For each date-filtered order, probe the bitset at o_orderkey. If bit is set, the order qualifies (EXISTS satisfied). ~9.7% of date-filtered orders expected to match.
o_orderpriority is dictionary-encoded uint8_t with 5 distinct values. Use int64_t count_array[5] indexed directly by dictionary code. Thread-local arrays merged at end.
Decode 5 dictionary values back to strings, sort 5 rows by priority string. Trivial — no real sort needed if dictionary is already in alphabetical order; verify at runtime.

semi_join_bitset.notes: 7.5MB bitset indexed by l_orderkey. Fits in L3 cache (44MB). Thread-local copies during build, OR-merged once.

aggregation_array.notes: Thread-local count arrays of 5 int64s, summed at merge.

parallelism.step1_detail: Parallel morsel processing of shared lineitem stream; thread-local bitsets, final OR-merge barrier
parallelism.step2_detail: Parallel orders scan with zonemap block skipping; morsel = 1 block (65536 rows)
parallelism.step3_detail: Fused with step 2 — each thread probes bitset inline after date filter, no synchronization needed
parallelism.step4_detail: Fused with step 3 — thread-local direct arrays, final summation barrier

notes: Steps 2-4 are fused into a single pass: scan orders block (zonemap-pruned) → date filter → bitset semi-join probe → direct-array accumulate. Step 1 must complete before steps 2-4 begin (barrier). Total memory: ~7.5MB for bitset + negligible for aggregation arrays.
